sections.html:
Norwalk sits in Fairfield County on the northern shore of Long Island Sound, inside the New York metropolitan area. It is the sixth most populous city in Connecticut, with 91,184 residents in 2020 and a 2024 estimate of 93,567.

The 2020 census counted 38,152 housing units, and 5.4 percent of them were vacant. Median owner-occupied home value for 2019 to 2023 runs about $535,000. With values at that level, the property tax bill is a real line item at any Norwalk closing, and an owner who sells with an unpaid balance needs a written payoff before anything else happens.

Norwalk is split into six taxing districts, and each carries its own property tax rate based on the services it provides. Two houses a mile apart can therefore be taxed at different rates, so find out which district your address is in before you quote a tax figure to a buyer.

The First, Second, Third and Sixth districts have their own elected officers, annual meetings and budgets. The Fourth and Fifth districts are not separate governments and make up the city proper. Some districts also run utilities:

  • The First Taxing District provides water to the Third, Fourth and Fifth districts.
  • The Second Taxing District covers parts of South Norwalk, East Norwalk, West Norwalk, Rowayton and Silvermine, and operates South Norwalk Electric and Water.
  • The Third Taxing District provides electric power to East Norwalk.
  • Eversource supplies electricity and natural gas across most of the remaining city.

Ask the Tax Collector whether your bill includes a district charge. If it does, the payoff letter should show it as a separate line.

Two offices deal with your tax and a third records your deed. The Tax Assessor sets the assessment, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Town Clerk files deeds and mortgage releases.

The Town Clerk page on norwalkct.gov gives the clerk's phone number and email, and the clerk's menu includes Land Records and a Property Alert service. Sign up for the alert if you want to hear when something is recorded against your parcel.

Call the Tax Collector for the current due dates, the installment schedule and any district charges, or read them off your latest bill. The office can also tell you whether a prior-year balance is still open on the parcel.

Bills do not stop being yours because they went to a previous owner or a lender. If anything is unpaid when you sell, it comes out of your proceeds at the closing table.

Norwalk has dozens of named neighborhoods, from Rowayton and Silvermine to South Norwalk, Cranbury and Oak Hills. They differ by shoreline exposure, train access and lot size, and buyers shop by those traits.

  • Rowayton, East Norwalk and South Norwalk each have a Metro-North station.
  • The Danbury Branch stops at Merritt 7, and Interstate 95, the Merritt Parkway and Route 7 all cross the city.
  • Silvermine holds the city's highest point, 315 feet above sea level.
  • Manresa Island is the site of a closed power plant that began conversion to a park in 2025.

Commuters to New York City value the rail stops, and a house near a station is often easier to market. A lot near the water may need different insurance than one on higher ground, so ask a lender or an insurer about your specific address.

sections.h2: Weather, flooding and what an inspector checks
sections.html:
Norwalk gets about 48.5 inches of precipitation and about 28.6 inches of snow a year. In 1955 three storms flooded Norwalk Harbor, and the coast, the river and the islands still define the city's topography.

Before listing, look at the roof, gutters, drainage and basement, and be ready to answer honestly about any past water. A buyer who learns about a wet basement from an inspector, instead of from you, will trust the rest of your disclosures less.

sections.h2: If you overpaid Norwalk property tax
sections.html:
Connecticut gives owners a limited window to claim a refund of overpaid property tax. Under Section 12-129, a written application to the collector must be delivered or postmarked by the latest of three years from the tax due date, any longer deadline the municipality sets by ordinance, or 90 days after a final court order or statutory process deletes an item of assessment.

The municipality can deny a refund when the same owner has another tax delinquency, and it applies the overpayment to that debt instead. Refunds that rest on an error of judgment by the assessors are barred. If you sold and think a Norwalk bill was paid twice at closing, send the collector a written request quickly, attach your closing statement and keep a copy.

A Norwalk sale can pay off unpaid property tax from the proceeds, so owing money is not a barrier to selling. The order of work matters, though, and it goes roughly like this.

  1. Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff, and confirm your taxing district at the same time.
  2. Check the land records at the Town Clerk for any recorded lien or unreleased mortgage.
  3. Have a closing attorney review the settlement figures before you sign anything.
  4. At closing, the title company pays the tax balance and any liens from your proceeds, and you receive the rest.

If repairs or tenant issues are slowing a traditional listing, an as-is cash sale is another route. It skips showings, repair requests and the wait for a buyer's mortgage approval, but you should still compare the net figure against a listing and read the contract closely before you sign.

faqs.q: How many taxing districts does Norwalk have?
faqs.a: Six. Each has its own property tax rate based on the services it receives, and the Fourth and Fifth districts make up the city proper.

faqs.q: Who do I call for Norwalk land records?
faqs.a: The Norwalk Town Clerk handles land records and recording, at (203) 854-7745.

faqs.q: Does Norwalk have its own utilities?
faqs.a: Parts of the city are served by taxing district utilities, including the Second Taxing District's South Norwalk Electric and Water and the Third District's East Norwalk electric service. Eversource covers most of the rest.
Check your latest bill or call the Tax Collector for the current schedule.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Norwalk house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff in writing first.
